CGBitmapInfo.doc: Component information for a bitmap image.

alphaInfoMask.doc: The alpha information mask. Use this to extract alpha information that specifies whether a bitmap contains an alpha channel and how the alpha channel is generated.

byteOrderMask.doc: The byte ordering of pixel formats.

kCGBitmapFloatComponents.doc: The components of a bitmap are floating-point values.

kCGBlendModeColor.doc: Uses the luminance values of the background with the hue and saturation values of the source image. This mode preserves the gray levels in the image. You can use this mode to color monochrome images or to tint color images.

kCGBlendModeColorBurn.doc: Darkens the background image samples to reflect the source image samples. Source image sample values that specify white do not produce a change.

kCGBlendModeColorDodge.doc: Brightens the background image samples to reflect the source image samples. Source image sample values that specify black do not produce a change.

kCGBlendModeExclusion.doc: Produces an effect similar to that produced by kCGBlendModeDifference, but with lower contrast. Source image sample values that are black don’t produce a change; white inverts the background color values.

kCGBlendModeHue.doc: Uses the luminance and saturation values of the background with the hue of the source image.

kCGBlendModeLuminosity.doc: Uses the hue and saturation of the background with the luminance of the source image. This mode creates an effect that is inverse to the effect created by kCGBlendModeColor.

kCGBlendModeMultiply.doc: Multiplies the source image samples with the background image samples. This results in colors that are at least as dark as either of the two contributing sample colors.

kCGBlendModeNormal.doc: Paints the source image samples over the background image samples.

kCGBlendModeSaturation.doc: Uses the luminance and hue values of the background with the saturation of the source image. Areas of the background that have no saturation (that is, pure gray areas) don’t produce a change.

kCGBlendModeScreen.doc: Multiplies the inverse of the source image samples with the inverse of the background image samples, resulting in colors that are at least as light as either of the two contributing sample colors.

kCGBlendModeXOR.doc: R = S*(1 - Da) + D*(1 - Sa). This XOR mode is only nominally related to the classical bitmap XOR operation, which is not supported by Core Graphics

CGCaptureOptions.doc: Configuration parameters that are used when capturing displays.

kCGCaptureNoOptions.doc: The system should use the default fill behavior, which is fill with black.

CGColorConversionInfoTransformType.doc: Constants describing how a color conversion uses color spaces.

kCGColorConversionTransformApplySpace.doc: Specifies a color conversion between one color profile and another.

kCGColorConversionTransformFromSpace.doc: Specifies a color conversion from a device color space to a color profile.

kCGColorConversionTransformToSpace.doc: Specifies a color conversion from a color profile to a device color space.

CGColorRenderingIntent.doc: Handling options for colors that are not located within the destination color space of a graphics context.

kCGRenderingIntentDefault.doc: The default rendering intent for the graphics context.

kCGRenderingIntentPerceptual.doc: Preserve the visual relationship between colors by compressing the gamut of the graphics context to fit inside the gamut of the output device. Perceptual intent is good for photographs and other complex, detailed images.

CGConfigureOption.doc: The scope of the changes in a display configuration transaction.

kCGConfigureForAppOnly.doc: Changes persist for the lifetime of the current application. After the application terminates, the display configuration settings revert to the current login session.

kCGConfigureForSession.doc: Changes persist for the lifetime of the current login session. After the current session terminates, the displays revert to the last saved permanent configuration.

CGDisplayChangeSummaryFlags.doc: The configuration parameters that are passed to a display reconfiguration callback function.

kCGDisplayAddFlag.doc: The display has been added to the active display list.

kCGDisplayBeginConfigurationFlag.doc: The display configuration is about to change.

kCGDisplayMirrorFlag.doc: The display is now mirroring another display.

kCGDisplayMovedFlag.doc: The location of the upper-left corner of the display in the global display coordinate space has changed.

kCGDisplayRemoveFlag.doc: The display has been removed from the active display list.

kCGDisplaySetMainFlag.doc: The display is now the main display.

kCGDisplayUnMirrorFlag.doc: The display is no longer mirroring another display.

kCGDisplayStreamFrameStatusFrameBlank.doc: A new frame was not generated because the display has gone blank.

kCGDisplayStreamFrameStatusFrameIdle.doc: A new frame was not generated because the display did not change.

CGDisplayStreamUpdateRectType.doc: Use these constants to determine which rectangles your app is interested in.

kCGDisplayStreamUpdateDirtyRects.doc: The union of both rectangles that were redrawn and rectangles that were moved.

kCGDisplayStreamUpdateMovedRects.doc: The rectangles for the portions of the display that were simply moved from one part of the display to another.

kCGDisplayStreamUpdateReducedDirtyRects.doc: The union is calculated and then simplified. This reduces the number of rectangles returned to your app, but it may report some pixels that were not actually changed.

kCGDisplayStreamUpdateRefreshedRects.doc: The rectangles for the portions of the display that were redrawn.

CGError.doc: A uniform type for result codes returned by functions in Core Graphics.

kCGErrorCannotComplete.doc: The requested operation is inappropriate for the parameters passed in, or the current system state.

kCGErrorIllegalArgument.doc: One or more of the parameters passed to a function are invalid. Check for NULL pointers.

kCGErrorInvalidConnection.doc: The parameter representing a connection to the window server is invalid.

kCGErrorInvalidContext.doc: The CPSProcessSerNum or context identifier parameter is not valid.

kCGErrorInvalidOperation.doc: The requested operation is not valid for the parameters passed in, or the current system state.

kCGErrorNoneAvailable.doc: The requested operation could not be completed as the indicated resources were not found.

kCGErrorNotImplemented.doc: Return value from obsolete function stubs present for binary compatibility, but not typically called.

kCGErrorRangeCheck.doc: A parameter passed in has a value that is inappropriate, or which does not map to a useful operation or value.

kCGErrorSuccess.doc: The requested operation was completed successfully.

kCGErrorTypeCheck.doc: A data type or token was encountered that did not match the expected type or token.

CGEventField.doc: Constants used as keys to access specialized fields in low-level events.

kCGEventSourceGroupID.doc: Key to access a field that contains the event source Unix effective GID.

kCGEventSourceStateID.doc: Key to access a field that contains the event source state ID used to create this event.

kCGEventSourceUnixProcessID.doc: Key to access a field that contains the event source Unix process ID.

kCGEventSourceUserData.doc: Key to access a field that contains the event source user-supplied data, up to 64 bits.

kCGEventSourceUserID.doc: Key to access a field that contains the event source Unix effective UID.

kCGEventTargetProcessSerialNumber.doc: Key to access a field that contains the event target process serial number. The value is a 64-bit long word.

kCGEventTargetUnixProcessID.doc: Key to access a field that contains the event target Unix process ID.

kCGKeyboardEventAutorepeat.doc: Key to access an integer field, non-zero when this is an autorepeat of a key-down, and zero otherwise.

kCGKeyboardEventKeyboardType.doc: Key to access an integer field that contains the keyboard type identifier.

kCGKeyboardEventKeycode.doc: Key to access an integer field that contains the virtual keycode of the key-down or key-up event.

kCGMouseEventButtonNumber.doc: Key to access an integer field that contains the mouse button number. For information about the possible values, see CGMouseButton.

kCGMouseEventClickState.doc: Key to access an integer field that contains the mouse button click state. A click state of 1 represents a single click. A click state of 2 represents a double-click. A click state of 3 represents a triple-click.

kCGMouseEventDeltaX.doc: Key to access an integer field that contains the horizontal mouse delta since the last mouse movement event.

kCGMouseEventDeltaY.doc: Key to access an integer field that contains the vertical mouse delta since the last mouse movement event.

kCGMouseEventInstantMouser.doc: Key to access an integer field. The value is non-zero if the event should be ignored by the Inkwell subsystem.

kCGMouseEventNumber.doc: Key to access an integer field that contains the mouse button event number. Matching mouse-down and mouse-up events will have the same event number.

kCGMouseEventPressure.doc: Key to access a double field that contains the mouse button pressure. The pressure value may range from 0 to 1, with 0 representing the mouse being up. This value is commonly set by tablet pens mimicking a mouse.

kCGMouseEventSubtype.doc: Key to access an integer field that encodes the mouse event subtype as a kCFNumberIntType.

kCGScrollWheelEventDeltaAxis1.doc: Key to access an integer field that contains scrolling data. This field typically contains the change in vertical position since the last scrolling event from a Mighty Mouse scroller or a single-wheel mouse scroller.

kCGScrollWheelEventDeltaAxis2.doc: Key to access an integer field that contains scrolling data. This field typically contains the change in horizontal position since the last scrolling event from a Mighty Mouse scroller.

kCGScrollWheelEventFixedPtDeltaAxis1.doc: Key to access a field that contains scrolling data. The scrolling data represents a line-based or pixel-based change in vertical position since the last scrolling event from a Mighty Mouse scroller or a single-wheel mouse scroller. The scrolling data uses a fixed-point 16.16 signed integer format. For example, if the field contains a value of 1.0, the integer 0x00010000 is returned by CGEventGetIntegerValueField. If this key is passed to CGEventGetDoubleValueField, the fixed-point value is converted to a double value.

kCGScrollWheelEventFixedPtDeltaAxis2.doc: Key to access a field that contains scrolling data. The scrolling data represents a line-based or pixel-based change in horizontal position since the last scrolling event from a Mighty Mouse scroller. The scrolling data uses a fixed-point 16.16 signed integer format. For example, if the field contains a value of 1.0, the integer 0x00010000 is returned by CGEventGetIntegerValueField. If this key is passed to CGEventGetDoubleValueField, the fixed-point value is converted to a double value.

kCGScrollWheelEventInstantMouser.doc: Key to access an integer field that indicates whether the event should be ignored by the Inkwell subsystem. If the value is non-zero, the event should be ignored.

kCGScrollWheelEventIsContinuous.doc: Key to access an integer field that indicates whether a scrolling event contains continuous, pixel-based scrolling data. The value is non-zero when the scrolling data is pixel-based and zero when the scrolling data is line-based.

kCGScrollWheelEventPointDeltaAxis1.doc: Key to access an integer field that contains pixel-based scrolling data. The scrolling data represents the change in vertical position since the last scrolling event from a Mighty Mouse scroller or a single-wheel mouse scroller.

kCGScrollWheelEventPointDeltaAxis2.doc: Key to access an integer field that contains pixel-based scrolling data. The scrolling data represents the change in horizontal position since the last scrolling event from a Mighty Mouse scroller.

kCGTabletEventDeviceID.doc: Key to access an integer field that contains the system-assigned unique device ID.

kCGTabletEventPointButtons.doc: Key to access an integer field that contains the tablet button state. Bit 0 is the first button, and a set bit represents a closed or pressed button. Up to 16 buttons are supported.

kCGTabletEventPointPressure.doc: Key to access a double field that contains the tablet pen pressure. A value of 0.0 represents no pressure, and 1.0 represents maximum pressure.

kCGTabletEventPointX.doc: Key to access an integer field that contains the absolute X coordinate in tablet space at full tablet resolution.

kCGTabletEventPointY.doc: Key to access an integer field that contains the absolute Y coordinate in tablet space at full tablet resolution.

kCGTabletEventPointZ.doc: Key to access an integer field that contains the absolute Z coordinate in tablet space at full tablet resolution.

kCGTabletEventRotation.doc: Key to access a double field that contains the tablet pen rotation.

kCGTabletEventTangentialPressure.doc: Key to access a double field that contains the tangential pressure on the device. A value of 0.0 represents no pressure, and 1.0 represents maximum pressure.

kCGTabletEventTiltX.doc: Key to access a double field that contains the horizontal tablet pen tilt. A value of 0.0 represents no tilt, and 1.0 represents maximum tilt.

kCGTabletEventTiltY.doc: Key to access a double field that contains the vertical tablet pen tilt. A value of 0.0 represents no tilt, and 1.0 represents maximum tilt.

kCGTabletEventVendor1.doc: Key to access an integer field that contains a vendor-specified value.

kCGTabletEventVendor2.doc: Key to access an integer field that contains a vendor-specified value.

kCGTabletEventVendor3.doc: Key to access an integer field that contains a vendor-specified value.

kCGTabletProximityEventCapabilityMask.doc: Key to access an integer field that contains the device capabilities mask.

kCGTabletProximityEventDeviceID.doc: Key to access an integer field that contains the system-assigned device ID.

kCGTabletProximityEventEnterProximity.doc: Key to access an integer field that indicates whether the pen is in proximity to the tablet. The value is non-zero if the pen is in proximity to the tablet and zero when leaving the tablet.

kCGTabletProximityEventPointerID.doc: Key to access an integer field that contains the vendor-defined ID of the pointing device.

kCGTabletProximityEventPointerType.doc: Key to access an integer field that contains the pointer type.

kCGTabletProximityEventSystemTabletID.doc: Key to access an integer field that contains the system-assigned unique tablet ID.

kCGTabletProximityEventTabletID.doc: Key to access an integer field that contains the vendor-defined tablet ID, typically the USB product ID.

kCGTabletProximityEventVendorID.doc: Key to access an integer field that contains the vendor-defined ID, typically the USB vendor ID.

kCGTabletProximityEventVendorPointerSeri.doc: Key to access an integer field that contains the vendor-defined pointer serial number.

kCGTabletProximityEventVendorPointerType.doc: Key to access an integer field that contains the vendor-assigned pointer type.

kCGTabletProximityEventVendorUniqueID.doc: Key to access an integer field that contains the vendor-defined unique ID.

CGEventFilterMask.doc: Specify masks for classes of low-level events that can be filtered during event suppression states.

CGEventFlags.doc: Constants that indicate the modifier key state at the time an event is created, as well as other event-related states.

kCGEventFlagMaskAlphaShift.doc: Indicates that the Caps Lock key is down for a keyboard, mouse, or flag-changed event.

kCGEventFlagMaskAlternate.doc: Indicates that the Alt or Option key is down for a keyboard, mouse, or flag-changed event.

kCGEventFlagMaskCommand.doc: Indicates that the Command key is down for a keyboard, mouse, or flag-changed event.

kCGEventFlagMaskControl.doc: Indicates that the Control key is down for a keyboard, mouse, or flag-changed event.

kCGEventFlagMaskHelp.doc: Indicates that the Help modifier key is down for a keyboard, mouse, or flag-changed event. This key is not present on most keyboards, and is different than the Help key found in the same row as Home and Page Up.

kCGEventFlagMaskNonCoalesced.doc: Indicates that mouse and pen movement events are not being coalesced.

kCGEventFlagMaskNumericPad.doc: Identifies key events from the numeric keypad area on extended keyboards.

kCGEventFlagMaskSecondaryFn.doc: Indicates that the Fn (Function) key is down for a keyboard, mouse, or flag-changed event. This key is found primarily on laptop keyboards.

kCGEventFlagMaskShift.doc: Indicates that the Shift key is down for a keyboard, mouse, or flag-changed event.

CGEventMouseSubtype.doc: Constants used with the kCGMouseEventSubtype event field.

kCGEventMouseSubtypeDefault.doc: Specifies that the event is an ordinary mouse event, and does not contain additional tablet device information.

kCGEventMouseSubtypeTabletPoint.doc: Specifies that the mouse event originated from a tablet device, and that the various kCGTabletEvent field selectors may be used to obtain tablet-specific data from the mouse event.

CGEventSourceStateID.doc: Constants that specify the possible source states of an event source.

kCGEventSourceStateCombinedSessionState.doc: Specifies that an event source should use the event state table that reflects the combined state of all event sources posting to the current user login session.

kCGEventSourceStateHIDSystemState.doc: Specifies that an event source should use the event state table that reflects the combined state of all hardware event sources posting from the HID system.

kCGEventSourceStatePrivate.doc: Specifies that an event source should use a private event state table.

CGEventSuppressionState.doc: Specify the event suppression states that can occur after posting an event.

kCGEventSuppressionStateRemoteMouseDrag.doc: Specifies that certain local hardware events may be suppressed during a mouse drag operation (mouse movement with the left or only mouse button down).

kCGEventSuppressionStateSuppressionInter.doc: Specifies that certain local hardware events may be suppressed for a short interval after posting an event.

CGEventTapLocation.doc: Constants that specify possible tapping points for events.

kCGAnnotatedSessionEventTap.doc: Specifies that an event tap is placed at the point where session events have been annotated to flow to an application.

kCGHIDEventTap.doc: Specifies that an event tap is placed at the point where HID system events enter the window server.

kCGSessionEventTap.doc: Specifies that an event tap is placed at the point where HID system and remote control events enter a login session.

CGEventTapOptions.doc: Constants that specify whether a new event tap is an active filter or a passive listener.

CGEventTapPlacement.doc: Constants that specify where a new event tap is inserted into the list of active event taps.

kCGHeadInsertEventTap.doc: Specifies that a new event tap should be inserted before any pre-existing event taps at the same location.

kCGTailAppendEventTap.doc: Specifies that a new event tap should be inserted after any pre-existing event taps at the same location.

CGEventType.doc: Constants that specify the different types of input events.

kCGEventFlagsChanged.doc: Specifies a key changed event for a modifier or status key.

kCGEventLeftMouseDown.doc: Specifies a mouse down event with the left button.

kCGEventLeftMouseDragged.doc: Specifies a mouse drag event with the left button down.

kCGEventLeftMouseUp.doc: Specifies a mouse up event with the left button.

kCGEventOtherMouseDown.doc: Specifies a mouse down event with one of buttons 2-31.

kCGEventOtherMouseDragged.doc: Specifies a mouse drag event with one of buttons 2-31 down.

kCGEventOtherMouseUp.doc: Specifies a mouse up event with one of buttons 2-31.

kCGEventRightMouseDown.doc: Specifies a mouse down event with the right button.

kCGEventRightMouseDragged.doc: Specifies a mouse drag event with the right button down.

kCGEventRightMouseUp.doc: Specifies a mouse up event with the right button.

kCGEventScrollWheel.doc: Specifies a scroll wheel moved event.

kCGEventTapDisabledByTimeout.doc: Specifies an event indicating the event tap is disabled because of timeout.

kCGEventTapDisabledByUserInput.doc: Specifies an event indicating the event tap is disabled because of user input.

CGFontPostScriptFormat.doc: Possible formats for a PostScript font subset.

kCGFontPostScriptFormatType42.doc: A constant representing a Type 42 font format.

kCGGradientDrawsAfterEndLocation.doc: The fill should extend beyond the ending location. The color that extends beyond the ending point is the solid color defined by the CGGradientRef object to be at location 1.

kCGGradientDrawsBeforeStartLocation.doc: The fill should extend beyond the starting location. The color that extends beyond the starting point is the solid color defined by the CGGradientRef object to be at location 0.

CGImageAlphaInfo.doc: Storage options for alpha component data.

kCGImageAlphaFirst.doc: The alpha component is stored in the most significant bits of each pixel. For example, non-premultiplied ARGB.

kCGImageAlphaLast.doc: The alpha component is stored in the least significant bits of each pixel. For example, non-premultiplied RGBA.

kCGImageAlphaNoneSkipFirst.doc: There is no alpha channel. If the total size of the pixel is greater than the space required for the number of color components in the color space, the most significant bits are ignored.

kCGImageAlphaOnly.doc: There is no color data, only an alpha channel.

kCGImageAlphaPremultipliedFirst.doc: The alpha component is stored in the most significant bits of each pixel and the color components have already been multiplied by this alpha value. For example, premultiplied ARGB.

kCGImageAlphaPremultipliedLast.doc: The alpha component is stored in the least significant bits of each pixel and the color components have already been multiplied by this alpha value. For example, premultiplied RGBA.

CGInterpolationQuality.doc: Levels of interpolation quality for rendering an image.

kCGInterpolationHigh.doc: A high level of interpolation quality. This setting may slow down image rendering.

kCGInterpolationLow.doc: A low level of interpolation quality. This setting may speed up image rendering.

kCGInterpolationMedium.doc: A medium level of interpolation quality. This setting is slower than the low setting but faster than the high setting.

CGLineCap.doc: Styles for rendering the endpoint of a stroked line.

kCGLineCapButt.doc: A line with a squared-off end. Core Graphics draws the line to extend only to the exact endpoint of the path. This is the default.

kCGLineCapRound.doc: A line with a rounded end. Core Graphics draws the line to extend beyond the endpoint of the path. The line ends with a semicircular arc with a radius of 1/2 the line’s width, centered on the endpoint.

kCGLineCapSquare.doc: A line with a squared-off end. Core Graphics extends the line beyond the endpoint of the path for a distance equal to half the line width.

kCGLineJoinBevel.doc: A join with a squared-off end. Core Graphics draws the line to extend beyond the endpoint of the path, for a distance of 1/2 the line’s width.

kCGLineJoinRound.doc: A join with a rounded end. Core Graphics draws the line to extend beyond the endpoint of the path. The line ends with a semicircular arc with a radius of 1/2 the line’s width, centered on the endpoint.

CGMouseButton.doc: Constants that specify buttons on a one, two, or three-button mouse.

CGPDFBox.doc: Box types for a PDF page.

kCGPDFArtBox.doc: The page art box—a rectangle, expressed in default user space units, defining the extent of the page’s meaningful content (including potential white space) as intended by the page’s creator.

kCGPDFBleedBox.doc: The page bleed box—a rectangle, expressed in default user space units, that defines the region to which the contents of the page should be clipped when output in a production environment.

kCGPDFCropBox.doc: The page crop box—a rectangle, expressed in default user space units, that defines the visible region of default user space. When the page is displayed or printed, its contents are to be clipped to this rectangle.

kCGPDFMediaBox.doc: The page media box—a rectangle, expressed in default user space units, that defines the boundaries of the physical medium on which the page is intended to be displayed or printed

kCGPDFTrimBox.doc: The page trim box—a rectangle, expressed in default user space units, that defines the intended dimensions of the finished page after trimming.

CGPDFDataFormat.doc: The encoding format of PDF data.

CGPDFDataFormatJPEG2000.doc: The data stream is encoded in JPEG-2000 format.

CGPDFDataFormatJPEGEncoded.doc: The data stream is encoded in JPEG format.

CGPDFDataFormatRaw.doc: The data stream is not encoded.

kCGPDFObjectTypeBoolean.doc: The type for a PDF Boolean.

kCGPDFObjectTypeDictionary.doc: The type for a PDF dictionary.

kCGPDFObjectTypeInteger.doc: The type for a PDF integer.

kCGPDFObjectTypeNull.doc: The type for a PDF null.

kCGPDFObjectTypeReal.doc: The type for a PDF real.

kCGPDFObjectTypeStream.doc: The type for a PDF stream.

kCGPDFObjectTypeString.doc: The type for a PDF string.

kCGPathEOFill.doc: Render the area within the path using the even-odd rule.

kCGPathEOFillStroke.doc: First fill and then stroke the path, using the even-odd rule.

kCGPathFill.doc: Render the area contained within the path using the non-zero winding number rule.

kCGPathFillStroke.doc: First fill and then stroke the path, using the nonzero winding number rule.

kCGPathStroke.doc: Render a line along the path.

CGPathElementType.doc: The type of element found in a path.

kCGPathElementAddCurveToPoint.doc: The path element that adds a cubic curve from the current point to the specified point.

kCGPathElementAddLineToPoint.doc: The path element that adds a line from the current point to a new point.

kCGPathElementAddQuadCurveToPoint.doc: The path element that adds a quadratic curve from the current point to the specified point.

kCGPathElementCloseSubpath.doc: The path element that closes and completes a subpath. The element does not contain any points. See the function CGPathCloseSubpath.

kCGPathElementMoveToPoint.doc: The path element that starts a new subpath.

CGPatternTiling.doc: Different methods for rendering a tiled pattern.

kCGPatternTilingConstantSpacing.doc: Pattern cells are spaced consistently, as with kCGPatternTilingConstantSpacingMinimalDistortion.The pattern cell may be distorted additionally to permit a moreefficient implementation.

kCGPatternTilingConstantSpacingMinimalDi.doc: Pattern cells are spaced consistently. Thepattern cell may be distorted by as much as 1 device pixel whenthe pattern is painted.

kCGPatternTilingNoDistortion.doc: The pattern cell is not distorted when painted.The spacing between pattern cells may vary by as much as 1 devicepixel.

CGScrollEventUnit.doc: Constants that specify the unit of measurement for a scrolling event.

kCGScrollEventUnitLine.doc: Specifies that the unit of measurement is lines.

kCGScrollEventUnitPixel.doc: Specifies that the unit of measurement is pixels.

kCGTextClip.doc: Specifies to intersect the text with the current clipping path. This mode does not paint the text.

kCGTextFill.doc: Perform a fill operation on the text.

kCGTextFillClip.doc: Perform a fill operation, then intersect the text with the current clipping path.

kCGTextFillStroke.doc: Perform fill, then stroke operations on the text.

kCGTextFillStrokeClip.doc: Perform fill then stroke operations, then intersect the text with the current clipping path.

kCGTextInvisible.doc: Do not draw the text, but do update the text position.

kCGTextStroke.doc: Perform a stroke operation on the text.

kCGTextStrokeClip.doc: Perform a stroke operation, then intersect the text with the current clipping path.

kCGEncodingFontSpecific.doc: The built-in encoding of the font.

kCGEncodingMacRoman.doc: The MacRoman encoding. MacRoman is an ASCII variant originally created for use in the Mac OS, in which characters 127 and lower are ASCII, and characters 128 and higher are non-English characters and symbols.

CGWindowBackingType.doc: The data type used to specify the backing option for a given window.

CGWindowImageOption.doc: The data type to use to specify the type of image to be generated for a window.

kCGWindowImageBestResolution.doc: When capturing the window, return the best image resolution. The returned image size may be different than the screen size.

kCGWindowImageNominalResolution.doc: When capturing the window, return the nominal image resolution. The returned image size is the same as the screen size.

CGWindowLevelKey.doc: Keys that represent the standard window levels in macOS. Quartz includes these keys to support application frameworks like Cocoa. Applications do not need to use them directly.

CGWindowListOption.doc: The data type used to specify the options for gathering a list of windows.

CGWindowSharingType.doc: The data type used to specify the sharing mode used by a window.

CGColor.doc: A set of components that define a color, with a color space specifying how to interpret them.

CGColorConversionInfo.doc: An object that describes how to convert between color spaces for use by other system services.

CGColorSpace.doc: A profile that specifies how to interpret a color value for display.

CGDataConsumer.doc: An abstraction for data-writing tasks that eliminates the need to manage a raw memory buffer.

CGDataConsumerCallbacks.doc: A structure that contains pointers to callback functions that manage the copying of data for a data consumer.

CGDataProvider.doc: An abstraction for data-reading tasks that eliminates the need to manage a raw memory buffer.

CGDataProviderDirectCallbacks.doc: Defines pointers to client-defined callback functions that manage the sending of data for a direct-access data provider.

CGDataProviderSequentialCallbacks.doc: Defines a structure containing pointers to client-defined callback functions that manage the sending of data for a sequential-access data provider.

CGDisplayMode.doc: A reference to a display mode object.

CGDisplayStream.doc: A reference to a display stream object.

CGDisplayStreamUpdate.doc: A reference to frame update’s metadata.

CGFont.doc: A set of character glyphs and layout information for drawing text.

CGFunction.doc: A general facility for defining and using callback functions.

CGFunctionCallbacks.doc: A structure that contains callbacks needed by a CGFunctionRef object.

CGGradient.doc: A definition for a smooth transition between colors for drawing radial and axial gradient fills.

CGImage.doc: A bitmap image or image mask.

CGLayer.doc: An offscreen context for reusing content drawn with Core Graphics.

CGPDFArray.doc: An array structure within a PDF document.

CGPDFContentStream.doc: A representation of one or more content data streams in a PDF page.

CGPDFDictionary.doc: A dictionary structure within a PDF document.

CGPDFDocument.doc: A document that contains PDF (Portable Document Format) drawing information.

CGPDFObject.doc: An object representing content within a PDF document.

CGPDFOperatorTable.doc: A set of callback functions for operators used when scanning content in a PDF document.

CGPDFPage.doc: A type that represents a page in a PDF document.

CGPDFScanner.doc: A parser object for handling content and operators in a PDF content stream.

CGPDFStream.doc: A stream or sequence of data bytes in a PDF document.

CGPDFString.doc: A text string in a PDF document.

CGPSConverter.doc: An opaque data type used to convert PostScript data to PDF data.

CGPSConverterCallbacks.doc: A structure for holding the callbacks provided when you create a PostScript converter object.

CGPath.doc: An immutable graphics path: a mathematical description of shapes or lines to be drawn in a graphics context.

CGPathElement.doc: A data structure that provides information about a path element.

CGPattern.doc: A 2D pattern to be used for drawing graphics paths.

CGPatternCallbacks.doc: A structure that holds a version and two callback functions for drawing a custom pattern.

CGScreenUpdateMoveDelta.doc: The distance, in pixel units, that an onscreen region moves.

CGShading.doc: A definition for a smooth transition between colors, controlled by a custom function you provide, for drawing radial and axial gradient fills.
